newsitem.title: FRANCE: Only 46 of 250 roadblocks left on French roads.
newsitem.headline: Only 46 of 250 roadblocks left on French roads.

text.p: Only 46 out of 250 roadblocks remained on French roads at 1630 GMT on Friday as truck drivers ended a 12-day blockade that had choked the country's highways, the national road traffic information centre said.
Barricades melted away rapidly after trade unions signed an agreement with employers on early retirement and reported substantial progress on pay and work-time claims.

"There are none left in the Ile-de-France region (around Paris), none left around Lyon and only three in the north, eight in the southwest, eight in the southeast, 11 in the east and 16 in the west," a traffic centre spokesman told Reuters.

Union leaders said they would put the outcome of talks at the Transport Ministry to members on the barricades, but many had voted with their wheels and headed for home even before the outcome of the negotiations was known.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe voiced satisfaction at the end of the dispute which he said had hurt many companies, adding he believed there had been a balanced solution to the drivers' legitimate demands.
The government agreed to help finance retirement at 55 instead of 60 for drivers and to issue decrees on full pay for all hours worked including loading, standby and compulsory rest time.
